purpose: Fill the gap between E149 (frozen image backbone) and E161 (raw waveform contrastive): build multi-band time-frequency maps from raw 18x1200 EEG with a fully deterministic rule (no statistics), then train a small CNN on Train session1 with supervised contrastive loss and feed the 256-d embedding into the unchanged E143 open-set protocol. Core question: can the Test diagnostic AUC beat 0.7578?

tfmap.aggregation: mean of log1p(|STFT|) over the frequency bins of each band, then mean over the bands of each image group
tfmap.layout: channel(18) x time(frames) matrix per image group, bilinear resize to 64x64; 18 channels keep the official channel order along the image rows (fallback layout from the task description, no invented topology)
tfmap.per_image_standardisation: subtract the per-image mean, divide by the per-image std over all 3x64x64 values (per-sample, no batch statistics)

encoder.output: raw linear projection, no L2 normalisation (E161 lesson: L2 normalisation collapses the representation under SupCon)

train.loss: supervised contrastive over within-task identity labels (positives = same subject, same task, other trials/views)
train.valid_metric: leave-half-out nearest-centroid identity accuracy on the 0.6<frac<=0.8 Train block

augment.note: EEG time is not reversible, so no horizontal flip

protocol.loso_known_block: 0.6 < frac <= 0.8, prototypes from fit_rows (frac <= 0.6) of the 19 enrolled identities
protocol.threshold: 5-block Train OOF score quantile at each acceptance rate

reporting.test_official: N/A: Test has no public labels; session is used only for the diagnostic AUC after scoring
